topic: VFR, IFR and Special VFR (Skyway Code)
summary: VMC minima depend on height and airspace class. At and above FL100 the minimum is 8 km visibility, 1,500 m horizontally and 1,000 ft vertically from cloud. Below FL100 it is 5 km with the same cloud distances, with UK exceptions for class D and class G at 140 kt IAS or less. VFR at night requires a cloud ceiling of at least 1,500 ft. Special VFR in a CTR needs 1,500 m visibility, clear of cloud, in sight of the surface and 140 kt IAS or less. Built from the Skyway Code pp.64-67.
src: The Skyway Code (CAP 1535 v4, Nov 2023), pp.64-67
sections: VMC minima
At and above FL100 / 10,000 ft (all classes): 8 km visibility, 1,500 m horizontally and 1,000 ft vertically from cloud
Below FL100 and above 3,000 ft AMSL or 1,000 ft above terrain, whichever is higher: 5 km, same cloud distances
At and below 3,000 ft AMSL or 1,000 ft above terrain (classes A to E): 5 km, 1,500 m horizontal and 1,000 ft vertical. Class F and G: 5 km, clear of cloud and in sight of the surface
Class D exception (UK): by day at or below 3,000 ft AMSL, in sight of the surface and at 140 kt IAS or less you may fly clear of cloud, with 5 km visibility (1,500 m for helicopters)
Class G exception (UK): 5 km may reduce to 1,500 m by day in sight of the surface at 140 kt IAS or less
VFR is not permitted in class A
VMC minima exist to avoid other traffic (e.g. class E cloud rules keep VFR from IFR traffic)
Other VFR requirements
A VFR flight may not take off or land in a CTR, or enter the ATZ or circuit, if the reported cloud ceiling is under 1,500 ft or ground visibility under 5 km. Request Special VFR instead
VFR flights may not operate above FL195 unless authorised
SERA VFR cruising levels are not mandatory in the UK
VFR at night (UK)
Same visibility and cloud rules as by day, except the 1,500 m class G reduction is not permitted
Cloud ceiling must be at least 1,500 ft
Be in sight of the surface at or below 3,000 ft AMSL or 1,000 ft above terrain
Never fly lower than 500 ft above ground or water, or 500 ft above the highest obstacle within 150 m. Over congested areas stay 1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 600 m
Submit a flight plan if leaving the vicinity of the aerodrome, and use an air traffic service if available
En-route obstacles 150 m (490 ft) or more AGL are lit at night
Special VFR (SVFR)
Allows flight in a CTR below VMC minima without complying with IFR. Subject to ATC separation from IFR and other SVFR flights
Minimum to accept a clearance: clear of cloud, in sight of the surface, flight visibility not less than 1,500 m (800 m helicopters) and 140 kt IAS or less
For take-off or landing in the CTR, reported ground visibility must be at least 1,500 m (800 m helicopter) or a cloud ceiling of 600 ft
SVFR at night is permitted in the UK. Some aerodromes have local flying areas with standard SVFR arrangements
IFR
You must fly IFR if below VMC minima (unless in a CTR with SVFR clearance). Class A is IFR only
IFR requires a valid instrument qualification
IFR flights fly at least 1,000 ft (2,000 ft in mountainous areas) above the highest obstacle within 8 km (5 NM), except for take-off or landing
Outside CAS, IFR cruising levels apply above 3,000 ft AMSL in the UK

cards.a: At least 1,500 ft, with 5 km ground visibility.

quiz.q: In Class E at FL100 or above the VFR visibility minimum is:
In class G by day at 120 kt IAS and in sight of the surface, the UK visibility minimum can reduce to:
quiz.why: 1,500 m by day, clear of cloud and in sight of the surface at 140 kt IAS or less.

quiz.q: The reported ceiling below which VFR cannot be used to land in a CTR is:
quiz.why: Below 1,500 ft ceiling or 5 km ground visibility, request Special VFR.

quiz.q: Special VFR minima for an aeroplane include:
o: 1,500 m visibility and 140 kt IAS or less
quiz.why: Clear of cloud, in sight of the surface, 1,500 m and 140 kt or less.

quiz.q: Which statement is true about night VFR in the UK?
o: The 1,500 m class G reduction still applies
Minima are the same as by day, except no 1,500 m reduction
quiz.why: The reduced class G visibility is not permitted at night.
